correctness.rationale: The signed antichain indicator convex hull has an exactly factored polar, with explicitly enumerated one- or two-norm layer vertices. Central symmetry and the farthest polar norm give the sharp inradius. Opposite tight inequalities force zeros in singleton blocks and constant coordinates in wider blocks. The remaining subset inequalities are equivalent to independent coordinate bounds because 1-sqrt(1-j/H) is strictly convex and vanishes at zero. Strictness for j>=2 proves that the only additional tangent facets occur at active box boundaries, counted by independent polar-vertex choices. The provided standalone checker verifies 27 profiles and 7,210 polar vertices but finite evidence is not an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general facet classification covers every defining normal, but does not by itself identify the set of centers maximizing minimum facet distance or the exact contact count for every boundary stratum. No broader theorem explicitly giving those quantities was found; this is not a proof of absolute novelty.

evidence: The farthest polar norm and hence the displayed centered inradius are direct consequences of Tsuchiya’s earlier polar-vertex description; this consequence is credited.

For a center of the same sharp radius, simultaneous opposite-facet equalities first force blockwise constants; then the remaining inequalities are precisely subset barriers. The strict inequality of the barriers for subsets of size at least two classifies the complete feasible box and only-one-unit-layer facet contacts.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior general polar list is not mistakenly treated as new. The center-box and contact-strata conclusions require an additional optimization/equality analysis, which was not presented by the inspected prior results. Historical priority remains provisional.

originality.rationale: The examined 2015 original obtains general facets and polar vertices, and consequently already implies the centered radius; no priority for these is asserted. The actual new object of comparison is a complete, canonical-metric classification of every optimal center and all contact-facet strata for the layered symmetric case. The 2023 work supplies ordinal-sum context but studies face vectors. The exhaustive equality constraints and strictly convex subset barriers are required to derive the box and its contacts. No inspected prior statement subsumes this classification; possible equivalent anti-blocking or Chebyshev optimization remains a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: A known general polar-vertex theorem already implies the centered radius, so the priority claim explicitly excludes that easy consequence.
Earlier optimization of anti-blocking symmetrizations or Chebyshev-center polytopes might encode the same box and contact formula without overlapping terminology.
Some publicly indexed geometric results were only available by summaries rather than accessible full primary texts.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural classification of all maximum Euclidean ball centers for the layered twinned-chain family, with unbounded-dimensional orthogonal center boxes, exact Euclidean side lengths and exact facet-contact jumps at each face. The center geometry is not encoded by a single inradius or ordinary face count, and supplies a motivated structural invariant in a canonical polytope realization.
